title: A maximal chain ending at a closed point of an integral finite-type scheme
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ be a nonempty integral scheme locally of finite type over $K$ [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $\eta$ be its generic point [def-sc-generic-point] and put $L=\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$, its function field [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Write $r=\operatorname{trdeg}_K L$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. Then there exist a closed point $x\in X$ [def-weil-closed-points] and points $\xi_{-r},\ldots,\xi_0=x$ forming a chain of specializations $\xi_{-r}\leadsto\cdots\leadsto\xi_0$ of length $r$ (that is, $\xi_i\in\overline{\{\xi_{i-1}\}}$ and $\xi_i\neq\xi_{i-1}$ for $-r<i\leq0$), with $\xi_{-r}=\eta$; moreover its residue field $\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field] is a finite extension of $K$.

source.place: Tag 02JX, lemma-alteration-dimension, proof of the equality clause: Jacobson generic fibre, finite residue extension, and the dimension formula over the field.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space] to $X$: its closed points are dense in the closed subset $X$. Since $X$ is nonempty, this dense set is nonempty. Choose a closed point $x\in X$. This uses only local finite type over $K$, not quasi-compactness or separatedness.

source.place: Tag 0478, lemma-locally-finite-type-Jacobson (2); Tag 02JX, lemma-alteration-dimension, equality proof, choice of a closed point in the generic fibre.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-closed-point-affine-dimension-data] to this closed point $x$. It supplies $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, its maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ representing $x$, the structural $K$-fraction-field identification $L=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$, and $\dim A=\dim A_{\mathfrak m}=r\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$. It also supplies the finite extension $\kappa_X(x)/K$.

source.place: Tag 02JX, lemma-alteration-dimension, equality proof: the closed point of the generic fibre has finite residue extension and local dimension r; affine-chart expansion using Algebra Tag 00P0, lemma-dimension-prime-polynomial-ring, and Morphisms Tag 01RV, lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-full-dimension-local-chain-contraction] to this domain $A$, maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and integer $r$. Choose the chain in $A_{\mathfrak m}$ supplied there and contract it to obtain $(0)=\mathfrak p_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak p_r=\mathfrak m$ in $A$.

source.place: Tag 00E3, lemma-spec-localization: prime extension and contraction; finite-supremum attainment and endpoint maximality expand the maximal-local-chain argument of Morphisms Tag 02JX, lemma-alteration-dimension, equality proof.

proof.text: In $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], a closed set $V(I)$ contains $\mathfrak p$ exactly when $I\subseteq\mathfrak p$, so $\overline{\{\mathfrak p\}}=V(\mathfrak p)$. Thus the strict prime inclusions of step 3 give distinct successive specializations. The generic point $\eta\in U$ corresponds to $(0)$: its closure in $U$ is $U$ by [def-sc-generic-point], so its prime lies in every prime, including $(0)$. The other endpoint is $x$. The open inclusion $U\subseteq X$ preserves distinctness and specializations, since closure in a subspace is the intersection with ambient closure. Index these points as $\xi_{-r},\ldots,\xi_0$. For $r=0$ the sole point is $\eta=x$. Together with the residue extension in step 2, this proves the statement.

source.place: Tag 02JX, lemma-alteration-dimension, equality proof: maximal local chain; elementary Zariski-topology conversion and reindexing.

lean.statement: theorem exists_generic_fibre_closed_chain {K : Type u} [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (.of K))] [IsIntegral X] [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of K))] : ∃ r : ℕ, @Algebra.trdeg K X.functionField _ _ ((functionFieldBaseRingHom (K := K) (X := X)).toAlgebra) = (r : Cardinal) ∧ ∃ (x : X) (ξ : Fin (r + 1) → X), x ∈ closedPoints (X : Type u) ∧ ξ 0 = genericPoint X ∧ ξ (Fin.last r) = x ∧ (∀ i : Fin r, (ξ i.castSucc) ⤳ (ξ i.succ) ∧ ξ i.castSucc ≠ ξ i.succ) ∧ @Module.Finite K (X.residueField x) _ _ ((X ↘ Spec (.of K)).residueFieldAlgebraMap x).toAlgebra.toModule
lean.note: Maintainer review fix: the residue-field K-algebra is the project's existing AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.residueFieldAlgebraMap (WeilConjectures.ZetaSeries), as in lem-kun-closed-point-field; the duplicate helper residueFieldBaseRingHom was removed. functionFieldBaseRingHom is the canonical composite ΓSpecIso.inv ≫ appTop ≫ germToFunctionField ⊤ (the same composite as the curve-local abbrev Scheme.functionFieldRingHom in WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.Curve.SerreDuality, which is not imported here because that module is a heavy curve-duality module).
